title: AI chat assistant detected
question: Does the site load an AI chat assistant whose users must be told they are talking to a machine?
method: Review when the static HTML loads a known chat or AI assistant (Intercom, Zendesk, Gorgias, Tidio, Drift, LivePerson, Ada, Crisp, Shopify Inbox and the like) and name it; found (none detected) otherwise. The disclosure appears inside the widget after JavaScript runs and cannot be checked; the duty often rests with the vendor that provides the AI system.

title: Machine-readable reservation of text and data mining
question: Does the store reserve text and data mining in a form machines can read, without shutting out search and shopping agents?
method: Classify what the store publishes: robots.txt groups for AI training crawlers, Content-Usage lines, /.well-known/tdmrep.json, a tdm-reservation header or meta tag, or reservation wording only in the terms. Found when a machine-readable reservation exists and the search and user-triggered agents scored in A2 can still read product pages; review when the reservation is in the terms only (not machine-readable under the 2025 Hamburg ruling) or when it also blocks those agents; found with a note when nothing is reserved, because reserving is a right, not a duty.

title: AI-generated product images marked
question: When product images carry AI-generation metadata, is it intact?
method: Fetch the main image of up to two sampled product pages (at most 2 MB each) and look for a C2PA manifest or IPTC DigitalSourceType trainedAlgorithmicMedia or compositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMedia in the embedded XMP. Found when an image declares AI generation; otherwise the check does not apply: missing metadata does not show an image is camera-made, because CDNs often strip it.
